summary: E! plans to premiere an eight-part documentary series about Bruce Jenner's transition from male to female on July 26, with each episode lasting an hour. Jenner recently disclosed that he is transgender after appearing with his family on "Keeping Up with the Kardashians." The article identifies several subjects it hopes the new series will explore, including his relationship with former wife Kris, his children, his role in the transgender community and viewers' reactions. Bruce and Kris announced their divorce filing in September 2014 after living apart, and Kris publicly expressed support following his interview with Diane Sawyer. E! executive Jeff Olde praised Jenner's courage and said the series would offer an unfiltered account of his experience, while GLAAD national co-chair Jennifer Finney Boylan will advise the production. Transgender actress Laverne Cox also voiced support and praised the humanity viewers saw in Jenner's interview. Jenner has six biological children and helped raise Kris's four children from her earlier marriage; he told Sawyer that the possibility of hurting his children concerned him most when discussing his transition. Several children have expressed support, including Kendall and Kylie, who said their father's happiness was what mattered to them. Although public reaction to the new series remains to be seen, Jenner told Sawyer that he hopes to use his visibility to make a positive difference.

Filipinos are being warned to be on guard for flash floods and landslides as tropical storm Maysak approached Saturday with steady winds of more than 70 mph (115 kph) and gusts up to 90 mph. Authorities took preemptive steps, including barring outdoor activities in some locales and precautionary evacuations, ahead of expected landfall Sunday morning on the southeastern coast of Isabela province, with the storm expected out of the Philippines by Monday.

A senior Defense Ministry official said al Qaeda fighters raided a prison in Al Mukallah, Yemen, early Thursday and freed at least 270 inmates, one-third of whom had al Qaeda links. Officials said senior al Qaeda figure Khaled Batarfi escaped and that attackers seized government buildings, including the Central Bank and radio station, before troops confronted them and most militants fled.

A Transportation Security Administration committee concluded that full screening of airport employees nationwide would not lower the overall risk to the public, according to a report released Monday. Full physical screening of employees also "is incapable of determining a person's motivations, attitudes and capabilities to cause harm, among other limitations." The TSA and most airports could not afford 100% employee screening, the report said. As a result of the report, TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions, including criminal background checks every two years for all airport aviation workers, screening of airline and airport employees traveling as passengers, reduction of access points to secure areas at all airports and increased random screening of aviation employees. Johnson requested the TSA study after a Delta Air Lines ramp worker and passenger at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport were arrested in December for allegedly smuggling guns onto flights to New York. Specifically, the TSA report said employee vetting should be strengthened by "updating the list of disqualifying criminal offenses, instituting continuous activity monitoring through the inclusion of additional Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and DHS data sources, and maintaining a national database of airport employees whose credentials have been revoked for cause." In addition, the TSA should expand the collection of domestic intelligence, which would include monitoring social media, and expand national reward programs to encourage employees to report security issues, the report said. Lauren Stover, security director at Miami International Airport, told CNN, "We support the findings of the committee and agree that there is no single solution in mitigating the insider threat, however we will continue our employee screening program as we believe that physical screening is a critical component to a layered security program."

Actress Mindy Kaling's brother says that he posed as a black man years ago to get into medical school and that the experience opened his eyes to what he calls the hypocrisy of affirmative action. But a Saint Louis University spokeswoman disputed the account, telling the Huffington Post that race never played a role in Chokal-Ingam's admission.

The Calabrese, an Italian Finance Police ship patrolling the Mediterranean near Lampedusa, has shifted from pursuing cigarette and drug smugglers to helping rescue migrants from Africa and the Middle East with its 12-man crew. Most of its crew participated in rescue efforts after a migrant ship sank off Lampedusa on October 3, 2013, killing more than 350 people; the Calabrese rescued four survivors. Crew members Gaetano Cortese and Enzo Idone described recovering dead children and a pregnant woman, memories that Cortese said return when they are home trying to sleep. The crew's safe, well-equipped vessel contrasts with migrants' accounts of fragile boats and rubber dinghies, often lacking food, water, shelter or trained crews, where survival may depend on rescue.

As Nepal grapples with an earthquake that has killed more than 3,400 people, Ronen Ziv worries about someone he has never met. Ziv says his baby is in a breech position, requiring a cesarean section. In the current chaos of Kathmandu, he worries his surrogate mother, Nafisa Shaje, will not get the proper medical attention required for a safe and healthy birth. Cila Tamir, Ziv's attorney, has been working with the Ministry of the Interior to try to bring Shaje to Israel.

Larry Upright, a staunch Republican, died Monday at a North Carolina hospital at 81, just one day after Hillary Clinton announced she was running for president. In his obituary, his family made just two requests: donate to Shriners Hospital for Children in lieu of flowers, and do not vote for Hillary Clinton in 2016. Daughter Jill McLain said it was natural to put that line in her father's tribute, telling CNN affiliate WSOC that he was very passionate about politics. Son Michael Upright said he knew his father would enjoy the request: "We know he's up there giggling right now, just laughing out loud," he told WSOC. His greatest joy was his family, and he was a former Shriner of the Year at the Cabarrus Shrine Club, according to his obituary. After retiring from the building automation industry, he became an avid golfer. The last few lines of his obituary spurred comments from across the country, including promises in the online guestbook not to vote for Clinton. Nigel Dufont of Kannapolis, North Carolina, offered his condolences but said he wouldn't budge on his support of Clinton, while an anonymous commenter said they would vote for Hillary if she was the best candidate.

The new "Fantastic Four" trailer, released Sunday, shows Sue and Johnny Storm's father initiating the project that gives the foursome their powers, their arrival in another dimension and a first glimpse of the villainous Dr. Doom. The movie, due out August 7, promises a very different take on the classic Marvel comics characters, played by Miles Teller, Kate Mara, Michael B. Jordan and Jamie Bell, and fans on Twitter had mixed reactions. The new trailer for "Jurassic World," out June 12, came out Monday morning and features even more of star Chris Pratt, with early word on Twitter pretty good. After a genetically modified mutant dinosaur escapes from an island theme park along with others, Pratt's scientist character takes charge of a mission to contain the dangerous creatures, and the trailer shows that the dinosaurs have learned to communicate with each other.
